name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 254 / NORTHERN DISTRICT / THREE SUERTES OF LAND, IN SAN JOSE GRANT / THE WIDOW AND HEIRS OF ANASTASIO CHABOLLA CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript title page, Case No. 777, 'Three Suertes of land in San Jose'

grantee.evidence: PDF p9 (transcript p3) names the alleged original grantee; a 200-dpi crop of the line reads 'Ma[z]ario Saez' - given name Mazario/Macario, surname begins with a capital that is ambiguous between S and L (register has 'Laez'). name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 386 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / LOS ANGELES PUEBLO LANDS GRANT / CITY OF LOS ANGELES CLAIMANT'; PDF p5 transcript title, Case No. 422, place named 'Pueblo Lands'. Register's 'City Lands Of Los Angeles' names the same claim in a constructed form (the case calls them pueblo lands / ejidos, claimed by the City as successor)

year.evidence: Exhibit B, the sworn translation of Exhibit A filed with the petition, ends at PDF p55 (Bancroft stamp 43): 'Mission of San Gabriel May 26th 1781. Phelipe de Neve. Filed in Office Oct 26th 1852'; its opening (PDF p53, stamp 41) reads 'For the foundation of the Pueblo of la Reina de los Angeles in the neighborhood of the River of Porciuncula...'. The petition, PDF p9 (stamp 4), says the same: 'in the year 1781, Governor Phelipe de Neve... gave formal directions (herewith submitted, marked A with a translation marked B) for the foundation of the Pueblo de la Nuestra Senora la Reina de los Angeles'

governor.evidence: The founding instructions are signed 'Phelipe de Neve' (PDF p55, stamp 43, verified on a 220-dpi crop of the signature line); the petition (PDF p9) calls him 'Governor Phelipe de Neve, Commandant General of the Internal Provinces of the West'

grantee.evidence: The claim is for the pueblo's own lands: petition PDF p9 (stamp 4) recites the 1781 foundation of the Pueblo and the 1786 delivery of possession of building and farming lots to the settlers by Governor Fages' commission (4 Sept 1786); the U.S.-era claimant is the City of Los Angeles as successor (PDF p1, p5). Register's 'Pueblo of Los Angeles' names the original holder, not the claimant

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 386 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p4 typed leaf 'LAND CASE 386 SD pgs. 205'; internal stamps '386 SD PAGE n'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd386.pdf. Board docket no. 422 (PDF p5, and '422' written at the head of many leaves)

outcome.evidence: Register's outcome cell is blank. Docket entry at PDF p8 (stamp 3) records that on 5 Feb 1856 Commissioner S. B. Farwell delivered the opinion of the Board confirming the claim, with the order following. District court and patent stages lie beyond the pages read

notes: The transcript's translation of Neve's founding instructions is dated in this clerk's copy 'May 26th 1781' (PDF p55, high-res crop). Quote it as the file reads; do not silently normalise it to the August date used in some printed accounts - I did not verify any external date. ⚠ This case file is INCOMPLETE: the front matter (PDF p4) notes 'Pages 1 to 205 (83 missing)'. Depositions read (Agustin Olvera, Jose Antonio Carrillo, Manuel Requena, PDF pp.13-24, stamps 9-19) concern the extent of the ejidos, not the founding date. Hoffman's 1862 row gives no year/governor/grantee for this claim, so the register is not contradicted by him.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 382 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / MONTEREY PUEBLO LANDS GRANT / CITY OF MONTEREY CLAIMANT'; PDF p4 transcript title, Case No. 714, place named 'Pueblo lands'. Register's 'City Lands Of Monterey' is a constructed form of the same claim

year.evidence: The claimant's title document is the acta of the Diputacion: PDF p18 (stamp 14) 'Sesion del 23 de Julio' and PDF p20 (stamp 16) 'Sesion del 24 de Julio', where 'se paso a tratar con respecto a los ejidos que la corporacion propone para la poblacion de Monterrey y se aprobo la siguiente demarcacion que hizo el Sor. Castro. Desde la desembocadura del Rio de Monterrey en el Mar, hasta el sitio de los Pilarcitos...'. Surveyor General Samuel D. King certifies (PDF p21, stamp 17) that these four traced pages are true copies of part of 'Secreta. de la Excma. Diputacion de la Alta California: Cuaderno limpio de Sesiones publicas para el ano de 1830' on file in the Spanish archives. English translation at PDF pp.24-25 (stamps 19-20), certified by W. E. P. Hartnell, State Translator, Monterey 4 Jan 1853. The petition (PDF p10, stamp 5) likewise pleads confirmation of the boundaries by the Departmental Legislature in July 1830

governor.evidence: Register's governor cell is blank, which is defensible: the Monterey ejidos were demarcated by the Diputacion, not conceded by a governor. For enrichment, the acta of 23-24 July 1830 is signed first by 'Jose Ma. de Echeandia' as Sr. Presidente of the Diputacion, then Antonio Buelna, Salvio Pacheco, Jose Tiburcio de Castro, Carlos Castro, and 'Juan Bauta. Alvarado, Secretario' (PDF pp.19-20, stamps 15-16)

grantee.evidence: The 1830 acta designates the ejidos 'para la poblacion de Monterrey' - the town/pueblo (PDF p20, stamp 16). 'City of Monterey' is the U.S.-era corporate claimant form used on the red label and in the petition ('the corporate authorities of the City of Monterey a Municipal Corporation', PDF p9, stamp 4). Right entity, later name; compare this register's own 'Pueblo of Los Angeles' / 'Pueblo of Santa Barbara' usage

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 382 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p3 typed leaf 'LAND CASE 382 SD pgs. 119'; PDF p2 curatorial note 'Pages 1-119, Maps nos 1175-1176'; internal stamps '382 SD PAGE n'; filename cubanc_lcf_sd382.pdf. Board docket no. 714 (PDF p4)

outcome.evidence: Register's outcome cell is blank. Docket entry PDF p8 (stamp 3): 'San Francisco Jany 22 1856. In the same case Commissioner Alpheus Felch delivered the Opinion of the Board confirming the claim (vide page 115 of this Transcript)', with the order at transcript p117. Later stages not read

notes: Register's otherwise-odd 1830 is CORRECT and well founded: it is the year of the Diputacion sessions (23-24 July 1830) that fixed Monterey's ejidos, certified out of the Spanish archives by the U.S. Surveyor General. Witnesses J. B. Alvarado (secretary of the Territorial Deputation) and Jose Castro authenticated the exhibits (PDF pp.13-16, 22-23). Hoffman gives no year/governor/grantee for court no. 382, so nothing conflicts.

name.evidence: PDF p1 red label: 'CASE NO. 242 / SOUTHERN DISTRICT / MUNICIPAL LANDS GRANT "SANTA BARBARA" / THE MAYOR AND COMMON COUNCIL OF SANTA BARBARA CLAIMANT'; PDF p6 transcript title, Case No. 543, place named 'Municipal Lands'. Register's 'Pueblo Lands Of Santa Barbara' is a constructed form; the file's own term is municipal lands

year.evidence: No grant of land dated 1834 exists in this file. The petition itself dates the origin of the settlement to 1782: 'That in the year 1782 the Spanish Government established the Presidio or Post of Santa Barbara, where the City of that name now is; that subsequently small tracts or lots of land were distributed at that place to settlers and discharged soldiers by the several Military Commandants... that subsequently this Presidio settlement was organised into a Pueblo or Municipality' (PDF p10, stamp 3). The register's 1834 does match the pueblo-organisation evidence put in on appeal: the translated 'Expediente containing the Election of the Ayuntamiento for the year 1835... Sta Barbara 21 Dec. 1834' and the ward elections of 7 and 14 Dec 1834 (PDF pp.125-131, stamps 70-75). So 1834 = the year the ayuntamiento/pueblo organisation is documented, not the year of any land grant

governor.evidence: Figueroa made no grant in this file. He appears as the officer to whom the 21 Dec 1834 election expediente was addressed: 'To the Political Chief, Jose Figueroa' (translation, PDF p125, stamp 70), signed Carlos Antonio Carrillo, President, with secretaries Joaquin Carrillo and Jacinto Lorenzana. Right officeholder for 1834, wrong implication if read as the granting governor: the claim was proved by ancient possession and municipal organisation, not by a Figueroa concession

grantee.evidence: The claim runs in favour of the municipality and its successor: petition PDF pp.10-11 (stamps 3-4) 'the land belonging to this said municipality, the dominion and ownership of which it has held for a long period of years... this said Pueblo, City or Town of Santa Barbara existed on the 7th day of July 1846 and continues to exist'; District Court confirmed to the Mayor and Common Council as appellants (PDF p194, stamp 139). Register's 'Pueblo of Santa Barbara' names the original entity, not a private claimant

land_case.evidence: PDF p1 red label 'CASE NO. 242 SOUTHERN DISTRICT'; PDF p2 typed leaf 'LAND CASE 242 SD pgs. 140'; internal stamps '242 SD PAGE n'; U.S. District Court wrapper 'No. 242 ... Transcript of the Record ... In Case No. 543' (PDF p18); filename cubanc_lcf_sd242.pdf. Board docket no. 543 (PDF p6)

outcome.evidence: Register's outcome cell is blank, but the file's course is unusual and worth recording: the Board REJECTED the claim, opinion of Alpheus Felch, 1 Aug 1854 (PDF p14, stamp 6): 'No effort has been made in this case to sustain any of the allegations contained in the Petition by evidence. In the absence of all proofs the claim cannot be confirmed. Rejected', with a decree that the claim 'is not valid' and confirmation 'be denied'. The city appealed (notice 31 May 1855, PDF p21, stamp 9; petition for review filed 8 Oct 1855, PDF pp.23-24, stamps 11-13). The District Court reversed and confirmed, decree entered 8 March 1861 (PDF p178, stamp 123, and the decree text at PDF p194, stamp 139: the Board's decision 'be and is hereby set aside and reversed, And that the claim of the appellants be held as firm and valid and is hereby confirmed as follows, to wit: bounded on the East by the Arroyo de Carpenteria, on the South by the sea shore, on the West by the Rancho of Dos Pueblos, and on the North by the Sierra, containing four leagues and no more'). The U.S. appeal to the Supreme Court was dismissed on motion, December Term 1863 (PDF p190, stamp 135)

corrections.year: 1834 is the ayuntamiento/pueblo-organisation year evidenced in the file (Dec 1834 election expediente, PDF pp.125-131); the case file itself dates the settlement's origin to 1782 (petition, PDF p10). No 1834 land grant exists in the file
corrections.governor: Figueroa appears only as 'the Political Chief, Jose Figueroa' addressed by the ayuntamiento in Dec 1834 (PDF p125); he granted nothing in this case

notes: Hoffman's 'confirmed' is right only because the DISTRICT COURT reversed the Board; the Commission rejected this claim outright in 1854. The four leagues confirmed in 1861 are consistent with the register's 17,826.17 patent acres (four square leagues is about 17,712 acres); Hoffman's '8 1/2 square leagues' is the claim as filed, not as confirmed. Decree quotations at stamps 123/135/139 were read from a 55-dpi survey render; they are legible and consistent with the 1861/1863 dates on the same leaves, but re-render those three leaves before quoting them in print.
